o1.biggest_strength: Puts the in-app checkout bug first as a no-test fix with the money sized (~560 orders, ~₹34 lakh gross margin), then ranks five evidence-tied tests with honest sample-size maths that admits page tests can only detect large lifts.
o1.biggest_mistake: Leaves blanks in customer-facing copy ('EMI from ₹[amount]/month', '[real rating] out of 10'), so it needs real figures filled in before the team can use it.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Fill every placeholder with real figures or clearly flagged assumptions and carry the in-app browser split through as a guardrail on each mobile test.

o2.biggest_strength: Clean, well-evidenced plan that leads with the checkout fix and the ₹34 lakh gross-profit figure, and names the pre-fix baseline caveat (0.70% before, ~0.81% after the fix).
o2.biggest_mistake: Applies a uniform 10% detectable lift to all five tests without adjusting to each metric's traffic and baseline, and ranks the hero-image test high despite admitting no chat data backs it.

reason: Both lead with the checkout fix and the money, but Output 1 shows its sample-size working test by test, tailors the detectable effect to each metric (6% for add-to-cart, 12% for mobile sizes) and picks a lower-ranked, better-justified final test, so it is the one I would hand to my team.
